sources.note: Decomposes three speaker settings -- the default Assistant, an assigned roleplay persona, and a narrated story character -- into sparse-autoencoder features at turn boundaries and pronoun tokens, and finds that roleplay personas retain an Assistant-associated feature core while differentiating from it across depth, where story characters never acquire that core at all.
sources.title: "Many Are My Names": The Anatomy of the Assistant and Its Personas via Sparse Autoencoders

sources.note: Compares chain-of-thought against answer-only supervision under a protocol where the two conditions differ in nothing but the training target, and finds the rationales buy nothing in-domain for strong backbones while buying 20 to 28 points out of domain -- with a human study attributing the measurable effect to language adherence and inspectability rather than to better reasoning.
sources.title: MathShikkha: A Controlled Study of Answer-Only and Chain-of-Thought Supervision for Bangla Mathematical Reasoning in Small Language Models

sources.note: Builds an expert-annotated Indian Supreme Court dataset in which each applicable statute is paired with the specific text span a legal expert says establishes it, and uses it to show that predicting the right statute and giving the right reason are separable abilities.
sources.title: PROSLEX: A Novel Dataset for Expert-Annotated Legal Statute Prediction for Indian Judiciary

sources.note: Trains open-ended medical question answering by scoring each response against rubric criteria that three frontier models independently agreed on, grading each criterion as correct, missing or wrong rather than yes/no, and recovering a gradient in groups where every response ties by judging the responses pairwise in both orders.
sources.title: ConRub-Med: Reinforcement Learning with Consensus Rubrics for Open-Ended Medical Question Answering

result.definition: How often independent annotators assign the same label, reported across 4 sources before anything is concluded from the labels -- and, in this archive, the practice that separates a validated instrument from an asserted one. The corpus's instances show both what it establishes and where it misleads. Two annotators at 93 percent raw agreement and kappa 0.85 establish that a labelling task is reproducible, which is what licenses scoring a model judge against them at precision 0.90 and recall 0.98. A legal-annotation study reports ROUGE-L overlap between two experts (mean 0.79) and calibrates its adjudication threshold on a blind 50-pair study rather than choosing it. And a rubric study reports raw agreement of 0.90 to 0.99 alongside chance-corrected kappas of 0.357 to 0.573 -- the gap being what happens when a class is near ceiling, which means a headline gain on such a dimension rests on a small number of discordant judgements. The archive's operative rule is that raw agreement without a chance-corrected statistic is uninformative when the label distribution is skewed, and that validating a model judge against annotators working from the judge's own criteria does not establish independence.
